subject: Re: Dedicated capacity packaging and hybrid pool proposal for Veridian Health
content:
From: Anna Kaplan <anna.kaplan@veridianhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@veridianhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity: initial workload and ask

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week. We ran the internal sizing exercise you requested and wanted to share our expected workload so you can recommend a Dedicated configuration and pricing. High-level:

- Production launch targeted early Q1 2027, US customers first.
- Average daily inference requests: 18,000 (writes/reads combined).
- Peak 95th-percentile concurrent sessions: ~45 at peak hour.
- Typical prompt length: 900 tokens (user message + system).
- Average completion length: 400 tokens.
- Expected QPS at peak hour: ~30–40 requests/sec (burst to 55 r/s for short windows).
- Persistence: long-running chat sessions with KV cache reuse; ~30% of requests hit cached prefix.
- Latency target: p95 < 500ms for streaming responses; p50 < 150ms.

We also attached the RFP that includes procurement terms and a short vendor questionnaire. What would you recommend for: GPU pool size (model assumptions: 70B family we discussed), reserve commit (12 vs 24 months), and pricing/discounting guidance?

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Kaplan
Director, Product — Conversational AI
Veridian Health
[Attachment: Veridian_RFP_Q3.pdf (application/pdf, 210KB)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kaplan <anna.kaplan@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial workload and ask

Hi Anna —

Thanks for the detailed numbers and the RFP. I ran these with Marcus and sketched two viable approaches (conservative and cost-optimized) based on Redwood's serving profile for ~70B parameter causal models. I attached a cost model that walks the math. High level: both options meet your p95 latency and give room for short bursts.

Quick clarifying Qs before finalizing:
- Will most requests be single-turn or multi-turn chats with long KV cache reuse? You mention long-running sessions — is the 45 concurrent sessions measured at conversation start or across active long-lived sessions?
- Are you planning to use streaming token-by-token responses for UX, or batched completions? (Streaming typically increases throughput needs slightly.)

Preliminary recommendations (short):
1) Conservative (SLA-first): 4x H100-80GB dedicated pool (reserved commit) + 1x burst node for scheduled spikes. Targets: sustained 40 r/s, p95 latency < 500ms; supports 45 concurrent long-lived sessions with KV reuse.
2) Cost-optimized (hybrid): 2x H100-80GB reserved + 2x burstable A10-class instances for daytime spikes and asynchronous batch jobs. Expect ~18% lower monthly cost vs conservative but requires a small policy for graceful degradation on extreme bursts.

Pricing / commit guidance (ballpark):
- 12-month reserved commit pricing shown in the attached sheet; 15% discount off list for 12-month commit; 23% for 24-month.
- We can include a $20k onboarding credit (one-time) for 12-month deals; larger credits available for multiyear.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for reserved pools; p95 latency guarantee with fallbacks to hybrid nodes.

I've cc'd Marcus for the technical sizing math and Ben/Laura for commercial follow-up. I can do a quick call later today to talk options.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: gpu_pool_cost_model.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 54KB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kaplan <anna.kaplan@veridianhealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T12:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial workload and ask

Anna —

Adding a bit of tech detail on the sizing so you can see the assumptions used in the cost model:

Assumptions used:
- Model family: optimized 70B causal model (quantized path).
- Effective tokens per request (prompt + completion): 1,300 tokens average (your numbers yield 1,300 after deduping KV).
- Average generation throughput on H100-80GB under Redwood runtime: ~800 tokens/sec sustained per GPU for this model/sequence mix (with prefix caching active).
- Cache hit reduces tokens to compute on ~30% of requests (we used 30% cache hit).

Sizing math (peak hour):
- Peak requests/sec requirement: 55 r/s bursts.
- Tokens/sec needed = 55 r/s * 1,300 tokens = 71,500 tokens/sec.
- Effective tokens/sec per reserved H100 (with caching) = 1,040 tokens/sec (because cached requests free ~30% of token work; we accounted for batch efficiency).
- GPUs required for peak burst ≈ ceil(71,500 / 1,040) = 69 GPUs.

That raw number assumes no request queueing and worst-case simultaneous bursts. For production we propose a mixed strategy:
- Reserve 6 H100 GPUs to cover sustained baseline (40 r/s sustained with headroom for p95 targets given batching and cache).
- Add an autoscaling burst pool (burst nodes using lower-cost A10-class instances or ephemeral H100 capacity) that can scale to handle the short spikes. In practice, with continuous batching and request shaping, a configuration of 6 reserved H100 + up to 30 burst GPUs (ephemeral) will meet your p95 target and keep committed spend bounded.

Rationale: the 69-GPU pure-reserve number is conservative because it assumes zero batching/queuing and all requests as cold starts. With KV cache re-use, streaming, and request shaping we can meet latency/throughput with far fewer reserved GPUs and rely on burst capacity for short peak windows.

I included an option to reserve 12 H100s if you prefer to avoid autoscaling bursts entirely — this provides a very comfortable buffer for expected growth but increases monthly committed cost substantially.

Happy to walk through these numbers on a call.

-Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Anna Kaplan <anna.kaplan@veridianhealth.com>

Date: 2026-10-12T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial workload and ask

Thanks Marcus — that helps. Two follow-ups:
1) The 69 GPU raw calc was surprising; can you share the burst model SLA and how quickly burst capacity provisions? We need <2 min scale-up for our busiest windows.
2) Commercial: Veridian prefers committed spend (12-month) but we need a stronger discount. Would Redwood consider a 20% discount on 12-month commit in exchange for a 30% higher commit baseline?

Procurement looped in; they will want the SLA wording and onboarding credits spelled out.

Cheers,
Anna

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kaplan <anna.kaplan@veridianhealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-14T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial workload and ask

Anna —

Appreciate the candid ask on discounting. Quick commercial counterproposal that balances your desire for committed spend and our capacity planning:

Offer A (Balanced commit):
- 12-month reserved commit equivalent to 6 H100s (baseline).
- 18% recurring discount off list for the 12-month term.
- $25,000 onboarding credit applied in month 1.
- Burstable capacity: guaranteed warm-up to 50% capacity in <90s and full provisioning to target in <8 minutes for ephemeral pool (we'll include warm warmers to shorten cold start tails).
- SLA: 99.9% uptime; p95 latency SLO in contract appendix.

Offer B (Higher commit):
- 18-month commit (hybrid finance), baseline 9 H100 equivalent.
- 22% recurring discount.
- $60,000 onboarding credit + one-week embedded integration support from our SRE team.

Notes: our burst capacity guarantees require a short warm pool and policy work (we typically keep small warmers spun to achieve <2 min effective scale-up for customer-facing SLAs). The 69-GPU number Marcus shared is a raw worst-case concurrent compute requirement; our production serving relies heavily on batching, KV cache, and request shaping so the practical committed baseline is much lower.

If you can confirm target baseline (6 vs 9 reserved) we can run the final pricing and produce a redline-ready SLA.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

- 20% recurring discount for 12 months (our internal target).
- $35k onboarding credit instead of $25k.
- Clear SLA appendix that spells p95 latency SLO and burst warm-up timings.

If Redwood can meet those three points we can send a redline within 48 hours and get procurement to sign the 12-month commitment.

Anna
